protocol.py: 6 biology problems (3 errors, 3 notes).

1. ERROR CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: master mix (tube A1 in slot 2)
   line 44:  p300.aspirate(20, tube_rack["A1"])
   At line 44 the tip went into master mix (tube A1 in slot 2) while it still carried sample
   1 (tube A2 in slot 2), sample 2 (tube A3 in slot 2), sample 3 (tube A4 in slot 2), sample
   4 (tube A5 in slot 2) and 3 more from an earlier step (this line did it 7 times). A tip
   that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this
   stock now holds material that does not belong there. Liquid drawn from it then took the
   unwanted material along into 7 other wells: wells B1, C1, D1, E1, F1, G1 and H1 in slot
   3.
   Affected: tube A1 in slot 2.
   Also reached 7 other wells: wells B1, C1, D1, E1, F1, G1 and H1 in slot 3.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 44 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [e4ceb628be93]

2. ERROR CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: 8 stocks
   line 49:  p300.aspirate(5, tube_rack[sample_well_name])
   At line 49 the tip went into sample 1 (tube A2 in slot 2), sample 2 (tube A3 in slot 2),
   sample 3 (tube A4 in slot 2), sample 4 (tube A5 in slot 2) and 4 more while it still
   carried master mix (tube A1 in slot 2), sample 1 (tube A2 in slot 2), sample 2 (tube A3
   in slot 2), sample 3 (tube A4 in slot 2) and 4 more from an earlier step (this line did
   it 8 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid
   it touches, so these stocks now hold material that does not belong there. Liquid drawn
   from them then took the unwanted material along into 6 other wells: wells C1, D1, E1, F1,
   G1 and H1 in slot 3.
   Affected: tubes A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and B3 in slot 2.
   Also reached 6 other wells: wells C1, D1, E1, F1, G1 and H1 in slot 3.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 49 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [b4160e805040]

3. ERROR PIPETTE-RANGE: 5 ul is below what the p300_single_gen2 can measure (20 ul at least)
   line 49:  p300.aspirate(5, tube_rack[sample_well_name])
   At line 49 the p300_single_gen2 is asked to draw 5 ul, below its minimum of 20 ul (this
   line did it 8 times). A pipette cannot measure less than its minimum: it draws the wrong
   amount, or nothing, and the volumes in this protocol only add up on paper. The simulator
   passes the move. Wells: tubes A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and B3 in slot 2.
   Affected: tubes A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and B3 in slot 2.
   Fix: Use a pipette whose range covers the volume (a p20 for 1 to 20 ul), or scale the
   reaction so every volume is at least the pipette's minimum.
   Source: Opentrons: pipette characteristics (volume ranges)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/pipettes/characteristics.html
   Source: Integra: pipetting tips (work at 35 to 100% of nominal volume)
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/united-states/en/pipetting-tips
   [091caef9858b]

4. NOTE NO-SAMPLE-INTO-REAGENT-WELL: (proposed) A tip that had been in a sample went into a
reagent
   line 44:  p300.aspirate(20, tube_rack["A1"])
   At line 44 the tip touched the liquid in tube A1 in slot 2 while it still carried sample
   1 (tube A2 in slot 2), sample 2 (tube A3 in slot 2), sample 3 (tube A4 in slot 2), sample
   4 (tube A5 in slot 2) and 3 more from an earlier step (this line did it 7 times). A tip
   that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, and the
   protocol never transfers that liquid into this well on purpose. A reagent is shared: the
   master mix, the enzyme or the primer in that well goes into every reaction on the plate.
   A tip that has been in one sample leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so
   a sample carried into a reagent well turns up in every well that reagent reaches, and a
   no-template control can no longer be trusted. Liquid was later taken out of the affected
   wells, and the unwanted material went along into 7 other wells: wells B1, C1, D1, E1, F1,
   G1 and H1 in slot 3.
   Affected: tube A1 in slot 2.
   Also reached 7 other wells: wells B1, C1, D1, E1, F1, G1 and H1 in slot 3.
   Fix: Use a fresh tip for each sample at line 44, or add the reagent to the wells first,
   while the tip is clean, and the samples afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [503cbcfee67c]

5. NOTE NO-NEGATIVE-CONTROL: No no-template control: 8 wells of master mix with a sample
   line 46:  p300.dispense(20, target_wells[i])
   At line 46 the robot starts putting master mix into NEST 96 Well Plate 100 µL PCR Full
   Skirt (slot 3), and 8 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on this plate
   holds the mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is
   contaminated, or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing
   on the plate can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, B1, C1, D1, E1, F1, G1 and
   H1 in slot 3.
   Affected: wells A1, B1, C1, D1, E1, F1, G1 and H1 in slot 3.
   Fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 20 ul of master mix and 5 ul of water in place of
   the template, and tell the plate map where it is.
   Source: MIQE 2009: a no-template control on every plate is essential
           https://gene-quantification.com/miqe-bustin-et-al-clin-chem-2009.pdf
   Source: MIQE 2.0 (2025): the no-template and no-RT controls, still essential
           https://academic.oup.com/clinchem/article/71/6/634/8119148
   Source: Bustin 2025: MIQE compliance remains patchy
           https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12154065/fullTextXML
   Source: Qiagen bench guide: PCR controls (no-template, no-RT, positive)
           https://www.qiagen.com/en-us/knowledge-and-support/knowledge-hub/bench-guide/pcr/reference-genes-and-controls/pcr-controls
   Source: Bio-Rad real-time PCR applications guide: controls in triplicate
           https://www.bio-rad.com/webroot/web/pdf/lsr/literature/Bulletin_5279.pdf
   Source: Thermo Maxima SYBR manual: the NTC contains all components except template DNA
           https://assets.fishersci.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0012933_Maxima_SYBR_Green_qPCR_Master_ROX_Sol__k0251_UG.pdf
   [12fee7f22fe3]

6. NOTE UNMIXED-AT-END: 8 wells never mixed after sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4 and
4 more went in (20% of the well)
   line 51:  p300.dispense(5, target_wells[i])
   At line 51 the robot added sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4 and 4 more to wells A1,
   B1, C1, D1, E1, F1, G1 and H1 in slot 3, which already held master mix (this line did it
   8 times). The addition was 20% of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the
   run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their
   own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated. A PCR plate is
   usually vortexed and spun down before cycling; if this one will not be, mix it.
   Affected: wells A1, B1, C1, D1, E1, F1, G1 and H1 in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix wells A1, B1, C1, D1, E1, F1, G1 and H1 in slot 3 after line 51: `mix_after=(5,
   20)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 20, well)`, with the volume about 80% of what
   the well holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to
   mix)
           https://support.illumina.com/ko-kr/bulletins/2017/03/best-practices-for-manually-normalizing-library-concentrations.html
   Source: Thermo PowerTrack user guide (a reaction plate not mixed well gives variable
   replicates)
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0018825_PowerTrackSYBRGreenMasterMix_UG.pdf
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   [e6314dab4554]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.
